provisions.title: Genetic Data Privacy; direct to consumer genetic testing company consent
provisions.quote: Separate express consent for transferring or disclosing the consumer's genetic data to any person other than the company's vendors and service providers, or for using genetic data beyond the primary purpose of the genetic testing product or service and inherent contextual uses;
provisions.appliesTo: "Direct to consumer genetic testing company" or "company" means any person that offers consumer genetic testing products or services directly to consumers or who collects, uses or analyzes genetic data provided by a consumer (W.S. 35-32-101(a)(x)); the chapter does not apply to HIPAA protected health information (W.S. 35-32-105(b)).

provisions.title: Genetic testing; informed consent to obtain, retain or disclose
provisions.quote: no person conducting genetic testing shall do any of the following without the informed consent of the individual or the individual's authorized representative:
provisions.appliesTo: Any person conducting genetic testing; exceptions in W.S. 35-32-102(b).

leads.usedFor: Find the genetic data privacy law

genetic.note: Informed consent is required to obtain, test, retain or disclose genetic data. Amended by 2022 HB0086, effective July 1, 2022.

crossCheck.note: W.S. 35-32-102(a), amended by 2022 Enrolled Act 8, effective 2022-07-01. HIPAA protected health information is excluded by 35-32-105(b).

facts.statutoryDamages: None fixed. Damages, injunction, and costs and reasonable attorney fees to a prevailing party, after a 60-day written notice and cure period (W.S. 35-32-104(b)).

provisions.title: Genetic data privacy; criminal penalty; private right of action
provisions.quote: An individual whose rights have been violated under the provisions of this chapter may bring a civil action to enjoin or restrain any violation of this chapter and may in the same action seek damages from the person violating this chapter.
provisions.appliesTo: Violations of the genetic data privacy chapter, W.S. 35-32-101 to 35-32-105.

provisions.title: Computer security breach; attorney general enforcement
provisions.quote: The attorney general may bring an action in law or equity to address any violation of this section and for other relief that may be appropriate to ensure proper compliance with this section, to recover damages, or both.

private_right.note: A person may sue only under the genetic data law, one narrow category. The breach notice law is enforced by the attorney general. No general medical records law with a private right was found.

crossCheck.note: Private suit only under the genetic data chapter, W.S. 35-32-104(b), effective 2022-07-01, after 60-day notice and cure. No fixed statutory damages. Breach law 40-12-502(f), from 2007 SF0053, is attorney general only.

facts.noticeDeadline: most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay

provisions.title: Definitions; personal identifying information
provisions.quote: "Personal identifying information" means the first name or first initial and last name of a person in combination with one (1) or more of the data elements specified in W.S. 6-3-901(b)(iii) through (xiv), when the data elements are not redacted.
provisions.appliesTo: Individuals and commercial entities that conduct business in Wyoming and own or license computerized data with personal identifying information of a Wyoming resident (W.S. 40-12-502(a)).

provisions.title: Personal identifying information; medical information
provisions.quote: Medical information, meaning a person’s medical history, mental or physical condition, or medical treatment or diagnosis by a health care professional;
provisions.appliesTo: Data element incorporated into the breach law by W.S. 40-12-501(a)(vii).

provisions.title: Personal identifying information; health insurance information
provisions.quote: Health insurance information, meaning a person’s health insurance policy number or subscriber identification number, any unique identifier used by a health insurer to identify the person or information related to a person’s application and claims history;
provisions.appliesTo: Data element incorporated into the breach law by W.S. 40-12-501(a)(vii).

provisions.title: Computer security breach; HIPAA deemed compliance
provisions.quote: A covered entity or business associate that is subject to and complies with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, and the regulations promulgated under that act, 45 C.F.R. Parts 160 and 164, is deemed to be in compliance with this section
provisions.appliesTo: HIPAA covered entities and business associates.

provisions.title: Computer security breach; notice timing
provisions.quote: Notice shall be made in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay, consistent with the legitimate needs of law enforcement

breach_health.note: Both elements were added by 2015 SF0036 (Enrolled Act 20), effective July 1, 2015. No attorney general or regulator notice is required by the statute.

crossCheck.note: Health data elements come from 2015 SF0036. HIPAA deemed-compliance clause 40-12-502(h) comes from 2015 SF0035. Both took effect 2015-07-01. Notice without unreasonable delay. No regulator notice required.
